sentences.text: 2. The prosecution case is that the accused who is the husband of the defacto complainant, while they were living separately, as per the advice of the counselor they started living together and while so, on 07.12.2023, he allegedly committed rape upon her against her will and thereby he is alleged to have committed the aforesaid offence.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the defacto complainant is none other than the wife of the petitioner and also that now the matter has been settled between the defacto complainant and the petitioner.
Therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent also filed affidavit, stating that the matter has been settled.
Moreover, from the allegations raised against the petitioner, it is revealed that the petitioner is none other than the husband of the defacto complainant.
On that ground also, the allegation of rape will not lie against the petitioner.
In the above circumstances, this Crl.M.C. is allowed.
All further proceedings in C.P. No.20/2024 on the file of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Aluva, arising from Crime No.1977/2023 of Elamakkara Police Station, stands quashed.
